text: Then I was like, okay, you know what? Entrepreneurship. This is what we have to do. Because Jalil noticed how his local mom and pop restaurants were all shutting down. Every year, 30% of new local restaurants closed down, yet global chains like McDonald's and Burger King keep opening thousands of new locations because they can afford to spend millions on software to manage and market their businesses.

I heard about this tool called Lovable and to be able to just write down your idea and visually see it, just that was gold for me. So with the help of his co-founder Hussain, Jalil built QuickTables, management software that lets local restaurants compete with industry giants. Really bring it down to the core. Mom and Pop style restaurants or even higher level style restaurants, they care about their food, they care about their food tasting good, they care about hungry people coming in and they're leaving well fed. What they don't care about is SEO and marketing and how their landing page looks. Fundamentally, I think it lets them focus on those things and then leave the marketing up to us. But for smaller restaurants, the rise of delivery apps created a challenge where restaurants are left with less and less customers inside.
